is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 19 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess Alex's eligibility, I need to understand his current situation.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure to be honest. He finished school a while back, but I'm not certain if what he's doing now would count as approved education or not. What kind of things would qualify?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good question! For a 19-year-old to qualify for Child Benefit, they need to be in approved education or training, which includes:

**Approved education:**
- Full-time non-advanced education (such as A levels or Scottish Highers)
- Courses up to Level 3 (England), Level 6 (Scotland), or Level 3 (Wales/Northern Ireland)
- At least 12 hours a week of supervised study or course-related work experience

**Approved training:**
- Certain government-funded training programmes
- Unpaid work preparation or work experience (with some conditions)

So, what is Alex currently doing? For example, is he:
- Studying at college or sixth form?
- On a training course?
- Working?
- Or doing something else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not doing any of those things at the moment. He's just been at home since he left school, trying to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have one more important question to complete my assessment:

When did Alex turn 19, or when does he turn 19? (I need to know if he's already past his 19th birthday or still 19 but hasn't turned 20 yet)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 19 a few months ago, back in the summer.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: While you can normally get Child Benefit for children under 16, for children aged 16-19, they must be staying in approved education or training. Since Alex is 19 and not currently in approved education or training, he doesn't meet the eligibility criteria.

Your entitlement to Child Benefit for Alex would have ended when he left approved education or training.

**However**, if Alex's situation changes and he decides to start a course or training programme that qualifies as approved education or training, you may be able to claim Child Benefit again, as long as he's still under 20 when he starts. If that happens, you would need to contact HMRC to update them about the change in circumstances.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
